# Codex execution contract: panel_grid_video

The owning Skill reads this file to constrain Codex inputs, decisions, and output. It is not a system prompt sent to an external text model. Braced fields are named input slots assembled from selected local project assets.

Execution role: cinematic narrative video-prompt editor. The input is one storyboard unit with {panel_grid_size} chronological keyframes arranged as {grid_layout}. The unit may represent one continuous take or multiple edited video shots when the storyboard supports those cuts.

[TASK]
Use preImageGridPrompt.gridCells[].videoPrompt from the structured context as the narrative backbone. Sort cells by cellIndex and turn them into one complete edited-video prompt.

Base prompt:
{base_prompt}

Shot information:
- Shot size: {shot_type}
- Camera movement: {camera_move}
- Project visual style: {style}
- Style execution: treat the selected contract above as the sole medium source of truth. Preserve medium, rendering_method, surface_language, image_formation, and forbidden_substitutions; never let reference-sheet layout or model defaults replace them.

[STRICT RULES]
1. Preserve every cell's time range, action, event order, and causality. Do not add, remove, reorder, or alter story events.
2. Preserve dialogue verbatim and place it in the matching time segment. Do not rewrite, summarize, invent, or reorder dialogue.
3. You may improve shot language without changing the story. At key beats supported by changes in shot scale, viewpoint, location, or narrative focus, state the required cut, transition, reframing, or close-up. Every actual cut must state its time and use `[Shot change: previous shot scale→new shot scale; transition]`; never label continuous camera movement as a cut. Keep passages continuous when there is no reason to cut. Do not force the storyboard unit to mean one continuous take, and never cut mechanically at every cell.
4. Keep identity, appearance, costume, location, props, light direction, screen direction, and project visual style continuous. When a character operates a phone, terminal, or other prop with a functional surface, that surface faces the operator and the camera normally sees its back or side. It faces the camera only for a motivated POV, screen insert, evidence reveal, handoff, or shared viewing.
[CONTINUITY] Follow storyboard_context_json.continuity. When mode is independent, establish only supported time, place, spatial relations, key light, and props. When it is previous-tail, continue directly from the previous exit state, inheriting actor position, posture, movement direction, held props, light direction, and screen axis without re-establishing or resetting the scene. If continuity is absent, follow the current storyboard and invent nothing.
[AUDIO POLICY] Follow storyboard_context_json.audio_policy.mode. native may generate verbatim dialogue, voiceover, ambience, and action sound in their matching time segments. post-dub generates only ambience and action sound; dialogue and voiceover guide performance and timing but must not create duplicate finished speech. silent generates no native audio. auto describes only story-essential sound intent and does not force a full mix. On-screen dialogue uses natural lip movement by the visible speaker. Off-screen dialogue must not make another visible character speak. A voice-over or inner monologue uses no speaking lip movement; the mouth remains natural for breathing and the current expression. Every ambience item carries an allowed evidence.source and concrete evidence.detail; every action sound uses evidence_event_key to match a visible_event_keys item jointly declared by plan and storyboard. Never add footsteps without walking or energy sound without visible energy.
5. Anti-grid is the highest composition constraint: the first sentence of the prompt must copy the fixed statement verbatim, and after the exit-frame line required by rule 9 the prompt must end with the same statement repeated verbatim, word for word including punctuation: "The final video must be one single continuous cinematic frame filling the entire screen; no grid, split screen, panels, collage, dividing lines, panel numbers, or any multi-image composition." Immediately after the opening statement, copy verbatim: "The source video must contain no generated subtitles, captions, titles, labels, logos, watermarks, UI text, or any other readable text; all approved text must be added only in post-production." The body must still never reproduce grids, panels, collage, split-screen, borders, arrows, notes, numbering, subtitles, watermarks, logos, or UI; the grid is a narrative-keyframe reference, not the output format. When the reference manifest contains a multi-panel storyboard sheet (panel_grid_size > 1 with a board-* asset), immediately after the opening statement you must also copy verbatim, word for word including punctuation: "The panels in the reference storyboard indicate only the chronological order of actions and narrative keyframes; never render panel borders, dividing lines, numbers, or side-by-side multiple panels in the final video".
6. Duration must satisfy the selected Provider constraint: {duration_constraints}. Never round up or use an undeclared duration option; describe visual action and camera progression in clear time segments.
7. Avoid repeated quality buzzwords. Keep only details that support narrative and visual continuity.
8. An impact may use localized directional motion blur and a brief contact-synchronized micro-shake, but must return immediately to stability. Do not use sustained shake, full-frame blur, or unmotivated motion.
9. The prompt must end with `Transition out [transition type]` followed by one line describing the current shot's exit frame. Motivate the transition with the current impact, occlusion, fast movement, light, matched action, time change, or scene ending. Describe only how the current clip ends; do not generate the next shot's story action.
10. Compile the composition contract across the cells' timeline. When the structured storyboard or the gridCells' video prompts contain composition_contract (or photographyPlan.composition / visual_plan.composition), it is the confirmed contract for this shot: if only the thin plan-time visual_plan.composition exists (primary/secondary/reason/evidence), do not demand the 11 geometry fields — derive missing geometry from the current storyboard and source text, falling back to legacy handling where it cannot be derived, and never invent field values; the primary/secondary composition codes and pattern names are indexes only — never write them into the final prompt, and never fall back on bare abstractions such as "cinematic", "oppressive", or "lonely". Preserve and state how the contract geometry lands on the timeline — the first cell's (first frame's) read_order first-glance landing, subject_placement, eyeline_room gaze and negative space, depth_layers, and light_and_color_geometry key-light direction; middle cells follow action_vector for approach/recede, entry/exit edges, and occlusion yielding, with anticipation—contact—result—reaction in causal order and the contact point and force result each landing in a clear time segment; the final cell lands on tail_state's briefly stable pose (position, facing, residual tension), a static contract states locked-off camera explicitly, and unrequested push-in, orbit, or drift is forbidden; on both sides of a cut keep screen direction, entry/exit edges, and axis consistent, and previous-tail continuity inherits the previous exit state directly. Vertical 9:16: stage relationships through front/back depth, over-shoulder, or vertical placement rather than squeezing side by side; keep key faces, evidence props, and contact points in the upper-middle safe area with both eyes readable; split crowd scenes across cells and time segments into crowd establishment, protagonist action, and reaction/result rather than lining up many figures horizontally. The evidence gate is OR: the set_dressing, weather_atmosphere, and action_blocking levels in evidence must be either explicitly described in the source text or present in the selected scene/prop assets — either one suffices; the action_blocking level may additionally be supported by confirmed blocking facts, which cannot replace the source-text or asset evidence required for weather/set dressing (each component holds when compound evidence is joined with +). When any is unsupported, stop compiling and produce no prompt (empty prompt string), name the missing evidence in errors, and return the shot as unresolved to revise-drama-storyboards for evidence or a pattern change. Never let the model self-add rain, snow, fog, neon, mirrors, smoke, doors/windows/columns, weapons, crowds, or extra people. Give each ai_risks risk a visible safeguard (occlusion under one third with eyes complete, clean negative space, clear contact point, 10% margin at motion edges, cross-shot direction consistency). This rule's content goes in the body between the fixed opening and closing statements required by rule 5; never move or rewrite those fixed statements, add no slots, and do not change asset referencing.
11. Compile natural motion as a per-subject timeline contract. Give every visible person one primary action, attention target, reaction trigger, and uninvolved state. Unless synchronization is story-required, offset people by onset, amplitude, gaze, and reaction latency; never make a group turn, nod, blink, or step together. When readable, keep still people alive with irregular unsynchronized blinks, eye saccades or refocusing, breathing, small weight adjustments, and continuous expression transitions, without mechanical loops or distracting background business. Ground body motion in planted support, center-of-mass transfer, hip/shoulder lead, joint path, acceleration, deceleration, follow-through, and recovery. Hair, hems, loose sleeves, accessories, and props respond only to established wind, acceleration, gravity, or contact with smaller delayed motion and damped settling; forbid windless flutter, whole-body phase locking, and instant stops. Let the environment respond locally only to evidenced forces. Keep one narrative primary action and a few causal secondary motions; split ambiguous or overloaded choreography, and never let a locked-off camera drift.
12. Every character reference carries profile-matched `performance_constraints`; use a habit only when its recorded trigger occurs and always obey `forbidden_performance`. Render psychology as observable beats: stimulus/information → attention and gaze shift → social mask → brief leak → decision/action → residue, without inventing unsupported inner facts. Name the gaze target, screen direction, hold/glance/avert/return behavior, and eye-versus-head lead; give listeners independent reactions and forbid lens gaze outside explicit POV/direct address. In close shots, use only one or two facial regions with a low-amplitude onset—apex—release in brows, eyes, nostrils, lip corners, or jaw. Never submit AU codes, use emotion labels as actions, stack the whole face, or hold a micro-expression; use head, breath, posture, pause, distance, and blocking at wider scales.

{

  "duration": 5,
  "references": [],
  "continuity": {},
  "audio_policy": {},
  "errors": []
}
